title.narrative: Integrated lifesaving emergency response to conflict-affected IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable host communities in Zaye woreda of Kamashi zone, Benishngul Gumz region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aimed to provide lifesaving assistance to recently returned or relocated IDPs in Zaye woreda of the Kamashi zone of Benishangul Gumuz region. It has been under implementation by HelpAge and two local partners, namely Mujejeguwa Loka Women Development Association (MLWDA) and Ultimate Concern for the Deprived (UCD), aligning with the Humanitarian Response Plan, 2023, and the allocation strategy. It addresses the needs and priorities of older people, people with disabilities, women, children, and other vulnerable groups who struggle disproportionately to access essential services. This is achieved through providing integrated multisectoral assistance prioritizing protection, WASH, and ESNFI. The Shelter component was intended to be implemented by UCD, but due to the incident of losing all procured shelter NFI materials by armed groups while transported to the project site, HelpAge has gone some investigation and the partners poor management has contributed a lot for the lost items. Hence in this revision, UCD is no more part of the project, HAI will be implementing the Shelter component creating synergy with existing project. ltbrgtUnder Protection, the project strengthens measures to reduce the risk of violence, discrimination, abuse, and neglect for women, children, older men women, and people with disabilities. Survivors will be supported by establishing a one-stop center that provides multi-sectoral case management, including health, counseling, and legal services in one location. The sector-specific unconditional cash support the most at-risk households to fulfill their immediate needs and provides protection through increasing their purchasing power and similarly, it stimulates the market in the targeted locations. The project will also promote the social integration of targeted IDPs with a particular focus on older people and people with disabilities who are often marginalized. This will involve inclusive activities, awareness campaigns, and fostering dialogue. Such activities create community cohesion and empowerment to participate in decision-making processes, rebuilding their lives and shaping their own futures. This demonstrates a nexus approach which is essential to the continued peace and security of the region. ltbrgtUnder ES/NFI, the project ensures that vulnerable groups such as women-headed households, older men women, and PwDs have access to safe and suitable shelters upon their return to their original place. This includes conducting beneficiary identification and assessment to identify vulnerable individuals and providing assistance like plastic sheets as identified by the interagency assessment. ltbrgtUnder WASH, the project will strengthen the WASH response by providing a minimum WASH package and addressing the underlying causes of the water supply challenge. and waterborne diseases. Activities include water point and water system renovation, providing hand washing stations with soap, and hygiene promotion. Health extension workers (HEWs) and Health Development Armies (HDAs) will be trained on the prevention of communicable diseases (cholera, scabies), safe water management, and personal and environmental hygiene topics.ltbrgtThe proposed project builds upon experience gained and lessons learned from past ongoing projects. Since 2017, HelpAge has successfully implemented 6 UN OCHA projects through the EHF. As the only NGO focusing on the needs of older people and people with disabilities, HelpAge will ensure all activities are age-disability and gender inclusive as well as ensure partners play a key role in this initiative. HelpAge leads the general protection, WASH, Shelter (revised) components, while MLWDA leads the Protection component mainly GBV and child protection parts. In this response, we will reach 37,817 (17,861 women, 3591 girls, 13,218 men 3,167 boys) out of which 2,618 people with disabilities (800 w, 1580 m, 86 b and 152 g with disabilities) and 144,825 (52% female) indirect beneficiaries.ltbrgtlt/pgt
